samples: This program defines circles, rectangles and points (circles and rectangles must have positive dimensions), computes each shape's area, and produces a one-line description of a shape that gives its kind, its size and its area rounded to two decimals. It can also pick the shape with the greatest area from a list, returning nothing if the list is empty. Its entry point prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, needing only console output and nothing else (no files, network or other side effects), so it works as a small demo or a starting template rather than a full geometry library.

This program defines circles, rectangles and points (circles and rectangles must have positive dimensions), computes each shape's area, and produces a one-line description with the area rounded to two decimals. It also offers a function that finds the shape with the largest area (or nothing for an empty list). Its main routine just prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, using only the console, so it is a small, safe demo rather than a tool for processing your own input.

This program models three kinds of plane shapes (circles, rectangles, and a point). Circle and rectangle dimensions must be positive, and each shape's area is computed. It offers a function that gives a one-line description with the area rounded to two decimals, and another that finds the shape with the largest area (or nothing for an empty list). Its main routine prints descriptions of a small sample set and names the largest, using only console output and no files or network, so it works as a small self-contained demo or a base to extend rather than a full geometry library.

This program defines circles, rectangles and points (circles and rectangles must have positive dimensions), computes each shape's area, and produces a one-line text description that names the shape and gives its area rounded to two decimals. It also offers a function that picks the shape with the greatest area from a list, giving nothing for an empty list. Its main entry point prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, so it works as a small self-contained demo and a reusable shapes library, needing only console output and no network or file access.

It offers a function that turns a shape into a one-line description with its area rounded to two decimals, and another that finds the shape with the greatest area, returning nothing for an empty list. Its main entry point just prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, needing only console output and no files or network access.
